input.summary: All three findings are fixed inside figures/; no application text changed. FIG. 3 no longer draws two independent routes to the outlet: the separate unobstructed bypass bullet is deleted, and the poppet bullet now puts the plain closure element between the bore and a plain passage that runs from it and opens through the upper band toward the outlet downstream of the dose chamber, that passage having no other opening to the bore. The flush bypass is therefore gated by the poppet, which matches the description and the whereby clause of claim 1, in which carrier liquid flows through the flush bypass only while the follower pin holds the poppet open; targets 26 and 58 continue to point at the interior of that passage and at the closure element. FIG. 4 no longer asserts that the metering sleeve's end lies inside the index collar with the collar overhanging it: the collar's right end carries the shallow curved edge indicating the round section, the unnumbered tube enters that end and is broken off at a conventional break line within the collar, and the brief states that no axial relationship between the tube's end and the collar is indicated, which puts this relationship under the same treatment the brief already gives the groove's hand, pitch and forming surface. FIG. 1's leader for numeral 64 now stops in the open space just outside the removable unit's outer boundary without touching the sleeve wall bands that carry 18, so the cartridge numeral designates the unit rather than the sleeve's end face. Space for the longer FIG. 3 bullet came from redundant wording in the same brief, including a repeated band qualifier and two phrases restating a part already named in the sentence, and I made comparable trims in FIG. 4. The numeral table, the per-sheet numeral lists, the Brief Description captions, the detailed description, the claims and FIG. 2 are unchanged, and the four sheets measure 2685, 2569, 2789 and 2778 characters.
reasoning: The FIG. 3 item was a topology defect rather than a shape one, so merging the two bullets was the fix: with the poppet standing between the bore and the bypass passage, and that passage given no other opening to the bore, closing the poppet actually closes the route to the outlet. That is the behaviour claim 1 recites and the specification explains, and the drawing now shows it instead of contradicting it.

I kept the bypass numbered 26 on the passage rather than moving the numeral, because the description attributes the flush bypass to FIG. 3 and the passage is still the structure that opens downstream of the dose chamber toward the outlet. Only the gating relationship changed, which is what the finding was about.

The FIG. 4 overhang had been introduced several rounds ago to keep the follower pin at one axial station across sheets, but the source gives only that the collar surrounds the sleeve and that the pin engages the groove. Breaking the tube off inside the collar keeps the surrounding relationship visible, leaves the pin in the groove where the rod bullet already places it, and stops the sheet from asserting where the sleeve ends relative to the collar.

For numeral 64 the earlier leader had been drawn to the sleeve's left end face, which put two numerals on one component. A leader that stops in open space just outside the unit's outer boundary is the standard way to designate an assembly, and naming the bands that carry 18 keeps the two leaders from converging on the same structure.

One note on the workspace: the FIG. 1 leader change was present, then the file showed the earlier wording again, so I reapplied it and confirmed the file now carries the assembly-leader wording at line 27.

Length remained the binding constraint, so the trims came from wording that repeats what each brief already establishes rather than from geometry, relationships or the disclaimers that keep undisclosed detail out of the sheets.

figures/FIG-3.md: trimmed a repeated band qualifier, a restated piston reference and a disclaimer phrasing to stay under the length cap

figures/FIG-4.md: the collar's right end carries the curved edge, the unnumbered tube enters that end and is broken off at a conventional break line within the collar, and no axial relationship between the tube's end and the collar is indicated
figures/FIG-4.md: trimmed the rod bullet and targets 36 and 42 to stay under the length cap
figures/FIG-1.md: the leader for numeral 64 stops in the open space just outside the removable unit's outer boundary without touching the sleeve wall bands that carry 18
input.prior_art_strategy: prior_art/INDEX.md lists no references and the Background cites none; the brief records that no prior-art search was run, so the art behind this draft may be incomplete and the independent claims should be re-tested against any later search. The claimed combination is unchanged. Claim 1 still rests on the axial ordering of the land faces and the port edges, which closes the concentrate port before the downstream land uncovers the carrier-liquid admission port so that separation is enforced by the moving geometry rather than by command sequencing, and on the flush poppet opened by the follower pin carried by the piston rod during the return stroke and closed before the waist reconnects the concentrate port. The FIG. 3 fix defends the second directly: a bypass permanently open to the bore would have depicted rinse flow independent of the poppet, which is precisely the feature that makes the rinse an unavoidable part of the same stroke and cannot be omitted, mistimed or deferred. The dependent ladder is untouched: the two directed rinse openings in claims 2 and 15, the flexible lip, the closed-port rinse interval, the express axial ordering of land faces and port edges, the index collar with its cam groove, three stop faces, detent and window, and the cartridge with threaded end cap in claims 10, 11 and 20.

I kept the bypass numbered 26 on the passage rather than moving the numeral, because the description attributes the flush bypass to FIG. 3 and the passage is still the structure that opens downstream of the dose chamber toward the outlet. Only the gating relationship changed, which is what the finding was about.

The FIG. 4 overhang had been introduced several rounds ago to keep the follower pin at one axial station across sheets, but the source gives only that the collar surrounds the sleeve and that the pin engages the groove. Breaking the tube off inside the collar keeps the surrounding relationship visible, leaves the pin in the groove where the rod bullet already places it, and stops the sheet from asserting where the sleeve ends relative to the collar.

For numeral 64 the earlier leader had been drawn to the sleeve's left end face, which put two numerals on one component. A leader that stops in open space just outside the unit's outer boundary is the standard way to designate an assembly, and naming the bands that carry 18 keeps the two leaders from converging on the same structure.

One note on the workspace: the FIG. 1 leader change was present, then the file showed the earlier wording again, so I reapplied it and confirmed the file now carries the assembly-leader wording at line 27.

Length remained the binding constraint, so the trims came from wording that repeats what each brief already establishes rather than from geometry, relationships or the disclaimers that keep undisclosed detail out of the sheets.

FIG. 1's leader for numeral 64 now stops in open space just outside the removable unit's outer boundary without touching the sleeve wall bands that carry 18, so the cartridge numeral designates the unit rather than the sleeve. I trimmed redundant wording in FIG. 3 and FIG. 4 to absorb the longer bullets, so the four briefs measure 2685, 2569, 2789 and 2778 characters.
